beliefs: f is even: f(-x)=f(x) in distribution, though individual noisy values differ by sign [E1, E2, E9]
For |x| >= ~1, f is essentially linear: f(x) ≈ 16.8·|x|, with slight sublinearity at very large |x| [E1]
There is a special interval roughly |x| < 1 where f deviates from the linear law, with a dip near x=0 [E3, E4, E5]
Inside |x|<1 the function is call-to-call noisy: repeating the same x gives different values each call [E8, E10, E11, E12]
The noise is not deterministic in x; scatter at fixed x (e.g. 0.05 gives -0.09 to 3.1) is comparable to scatter across nearby x [E11, E12]
The mean of f in the special interval rises roughly linearly from ~0 at 0 to ~16.8 at 1 [E5, E7, E8]
Noise magnitude grows with |x| in the special interval (small near 0, larger near 1) [E8, E11, E12]
The transition from noisy special region to clean linear regime happens around |x|≈1 [E3, E4, E7]
notes: Confirmed the near-zero region is call-to-call noise (repeats at same x scatter widely), so predict() should output the mean ramp 16.8|x| for |x|<1 (best point estimate under noise) and the linear law for |x|>=1; removed the spurious x^1.05 exponent that hurt matches.
